summary: Learn WCAG, assistive technology testing, AI risk controls, and accessible procurement through practical workshops. Build evidence-based digital services.
lede: Training in accessible, inclusive AI helps product, design, procurement, and assurance teams assess AI-enabled services for people with disabilities. You’ll practise applying WCAG 2.2 criteria, mapping user journeys, testing keyboard and screen-reader access, and identifying AI-related exclusion risks. Exercises develop practical artefacts, including accessibility test records, risk registers, and procurement scorecards for use in service decisions and reviews.
audienceIntro: This responsible AI and digital accessibility training suits professionals who shape, build, buy, govern, or assure AI-enabled digital services across public and private organizations. It supports early-career and experienced practitioners who need a shared vocabulary and practical artefacts, while advanced technical engineering remains outside the course scope.
prerequisites: Working experience in digital product delivery, UX, service design, AI ownership, procurement, compliance, or digital governance is recommended. You do not need to code or hold an accessibility certification. Familiarity with basic web interfaces and organizational risk processes will help, but the course introduces WCAG 2.2, NIST AI RMF, and assistive technology workflows from a practical foundation. Advanced topics such as AI model engineering, production deployment, and detailed legal interpretation receive conceptual or operational coverage. The course focuses on applying accessibility requirements, evaluating evidence, and designing governance artefacts.
topics: Generative AI at work & AI copilots
